facts.text: The controller imports Supervisor from Webots' embedded controller module, not from a serial, USB, VISA or vendor transport library

The position threshold is 0.3 and the pole-angle threshold is 0.2 rad; the observation upper bound is twice each threshold for the position and angle entries and float32 maximum for the two velocity entries
Each action sets all four wheel target velocities to 1.3 rad/s when the action is 1 and to -1.3 rad/s otherwise
The observation is [robot position z, robot velocity z, position-sensor value, POLE_ENDPOINT angular velocity z]
The episode is done when the position or the pole angle passes its threshold
The reward is 0 on the step that reports done and 1 otherwise
reset restarts the simulation physics and the world, then rebinds the four wheels and the position sensor
reset takes no seed or options and returns a fixed four-zero observation
step returns the legacy four-tuple (state, reward, done, info)
The constructor default max_episode_steps is 1000 and is stored in EnvSpec(id='WebotsEnv-v0'); reset and step never enforce a time limit or truncate
The world file is a Webots R2021a world
The world places a Pioneer3at with controller gym_controller and supervisor TRUE
The balancing pole is attached through a HingeJoint with a PositionSensor
The pole is a 0.5 m cylinder with a 0.1 m ball at POLE_ENDPOINT whose mass is 0.2 kg

determinism.notes: the upstream reset always starts from the fixed four-zero observation and the fake has no randomness, so the same action sequence from a fresh world gives the same state hashes; cap.world.seed.v1 is recorded by the bridge but does not change the fixed reset

gaps: no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, wheel slip, motor model, sensor noise or gravity: each step is a discrete analytic update, and the real trajectories come from Webots' physics, which was not run
timestep_ms is 0 because the Webots basic time step is not stated in the clone (WorldInfo has no basicTimeStep); one tick is one controller step, not a physical duration
the fake reset reproduces the upstream fixed four-zero observation but not simulationReset or simulationResetPhysics, and the fake was never compared with a Webots run
no physical device is modelled and there is no hardware backend
snapshot and restore are not offered: the upstream class exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop no step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the last observation stays readable
